title: Warm Tangy Chinese Oats Twice Cooked Pork
description: A tangy and comforting Chinese dish featuring porridge oats and twice-cooked pork, perfect for a hangover cure, and can be made vegetarian-friendly by substituting the pork with extra firm tofu or portobello mushrooms. This dish is a variation of a traditional Chinese recipe, adapted to include oats for added texture and nutrition.

ingredients.name: porridge oats
ingredients.notes: rolled oats or old fashioned oats work best

ingredients.name: pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: or extra firm tofu or portobello mushrooms for vegetarian option

instructions: In a large pot, bring 4 cups of water to a boil and add the oats, reducing heat to low and simmering for 10 minutes.
While the oats are cooking, heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the sliced ginger and minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork shoulder or vegetarian substitute to the pan and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and honey to the pan and stir to combine, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and let the pork or substitute cook in the sauce for 10 minutes, or until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Fluff the cooked oats with a fork and stir in the chopped scallions and cooked pork or substitute.
Season the oats with salt and pepper to taste, and serve hot.
Garnish with additional scallions and a drizzle of soy sauce, if desired.
Let the dish rest for a few minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before serving.
